body:
## Pull request overview

This PR upgrades the `LookupField` experience to support dynamic option loading (via `DataSource.find()`), richer option rendering, keyboard navigation, quick-create, and improved states (loading/error/empty) so lookup dialogs work with real backends (not only static `options`) and integrate cleanly with the console form renderer.

**Changes:**
- Enhanced `LookupField` to fetch options dynamically from a `DataSource`, with debounced search, pagination hint, keyboard navigation, and quick-create UI.
- Updated the form renderer to read `dataSource` from `SchemaRendererContext` and pass it down to field widgets.
- Expanded documentation and roadmap to reflect the new Lookup capabilities.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 7 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx | Adds dynamic DataSource-based fetching, debounced search, keyboard nav, quick-create, and wrapper field metadata unwrapping. |
| packages/fields/src/complex-widgets.test.tsx | Adds tests for dynamic Lookup behavior (fetching, states, search debounce, selection, wrapper metadata, ObjectStack `reference`). |
| packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx | Propagates `dataSource` from `SchemaRendererContext` down into rendered field widgets. |
| content/docs/fields/lookup.mdx | Documents dynamic DataSource loading, search behavior, description field, keyboard nav, and quick-create. |
| ROADMAP.md | Marks Lookup dynamic loading + UX enhancements as completed. |
</details>

When the dialog closes, the debounce timer isn’t cleared and `fetchedOptions/totalCount` aren’t reset. This can trigger fetches after close and show stale options immediately on the next open while a new request is in-flight. Clearing any pending debounce on close and resetting fetched state (or guarding `fetchLookupData` with `isOpen`) would prevent these stale/late updates.

`onCreateNew` is read from `props` or `lookupField`, but not from `fieldMeta`. In the createFieldRenderer wrapper case, quick-create configured on the inner `field.field` metadata won’t be detected. Consider falling back to `fieldMeta?.onCreateNew` as well so wrapper and non-wrapper usage behave consistently.
```suggestion
    (props as any).onCreateNew ?? lookupField?.onCreateNew ?? fieldMeta?.onCreateNew;
```

Passing `dataSource: contextDataSource` here will override any per-field `dataSource` present in `fieldProps` and also forwards `dataSource` to built-in inputs/selects (which can end up as an unknown DOM prop). Prefer preserving precedence (`fieldProps.dataSource ?? contextDataSource`) and only including the prop when defined (e.g., conditional spread) so standard DOM inputs don’t receive it.

This section states that Lookup can obtain a `DataSource` via `SchemaRendererContext`, but the current LookupField implementation relies on a dynamic `require('@object-ui/react')` fallback that won’t resolve under ESM-only `@object-ui/react` exports. If the intended mechanism is “form renderer passes `dataSource` down”, consider updating the docs to describe that flow (or update the widget to use a real context import).

`SchemaRendererContext` resolution via `require('@object-ui/react')` will not work reliably with the current `@object-ui/react` packaging (ESM-only exports, no `require` entry), so this context fallback will always be used and `ctx?.dataSource` will stay null. Either remove this dynamic-require path and rely on the `dataSource` prop (now provided by the form renderer), or add an explicit dependency/peerDependency on `@object-ui/react` and use a normal import so context-based DataSource actually works.
```suggestion
 * SchemaRendererContext placeholder.
 *
 * LookupField primarily relies on the `dataSource` prop provided by the
 * form renderer. This local context is kept for compatibility with any
 * existing `useContext(SchemaRendererContext)` usage but always defaults
 * to `null` within this package.
 */
const SchemaRendererContext = React.createContext<any>(null);
```
